name: Greek Chickpea Fritters (Revithokeftedes)

cookwares.name: 10-inch cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

ingredients.name: fresh flat leaf parsley, finely chopped

instructions.primary_message: In a food processor, gently pulse chickpeas. Alternatively, mash with a potato masher, a fork, or your hands. Aim for a mixture with about 3/4 mashed and the rest whole/broken.

In a large bowl, combine mashed chickpeas, parsley, dill, onion, oregano, thyme or marjoram, salt, pepper, flour, and egg. Use a spoon to stir until combined gently. Refrigerate mixture until batter is set enough to scoop and rest on a spoon, about 15 minutes.

Once mixture has rested, line a rimmed baking sheet with a double layer of paper towels and set aside. In a 10-inch cast iron skillet or Dutch oven, add oil (oil should measure 1 to 1 1/2 inches deep) and heat on medium-high until oil registers 350°F on an instant-read or deep-fry thermometer. Once oil reaches 350°F, lower heat to medium.
Using a 1.75-ounce cookie scoop (or 2 tablespoons), drop 6 portions of batter into pan, evenly spaced apart, using a spoon to gently transfer batter into hot oil.

Note that some loud, vigorous bubbling is common when fritters first contact the oil. Use the back of a fork or spatula to gently press each patty to slightly flatten. Fry fritters for 10 seconds, then give a gentle nudge underneath with a fork or spatula to ensure they are not sticking to bottom of pan. Continue to fry, flipping occasionally for even browning and adjusting heat as needed to maintain oil temperature around 300 to 350°F (150 to 175°C), until deep golden brown, 8 to 12 minutes total.
Use a slotted spoon or spatula to transfer fritters to a prepared sheet lined with paper towels. Sprinkle with salt.

Return oil to 350°F, adjusting heat as needed, and repeat frying fritters in batches of 5 to 6 at a time for a total of about 16 fritters. Let the last batch sit for 2 minutes after removing from oil. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

description: These Greek chickpea fritters, known as revithokeftedes, are crisp, fluffy, herb-packed, and easy to make with pantry staples.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 teaspoons dried thyme or marjoram, optional; Optional fresh lemon wedges, for serving

Notes: Choose an oil with a high smoke point. I recommend safflower, sunflower, or avocado oil, as they are neutral in flavor.

Make-ahead and storage: The fritters are best served immediately, but leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat on a parchment paper-lined rimmed baking sheet in a 350°F oven until recrisped and heated through, 5 to 7 minutes.
author: Sharon Brenner
